what_happened: Drain-29 stopped because job 3v30 failed twice during planning at the $8 per-job budget cap. Raising the cap is a config change, and config can only change through a job. If drain had kept retrying 3v30, it would have hit the same cap each time. The the person running Athena ran the budget-raise job (0n3b) by hand with `athena go` and land.sh, ahead of the queue, so the hard jobs could proceed. This was an the person running Athena intervention in which the the person running Athena did the work.
cause: The per-job budget is a fixed config value that Athena does not compare with what hard jobs need. A job that spends its cap in planning fails and is retried under the same cap. Nothing tells drain that the cap is the cause, so drain cannot hold the job or raise a flag. Because config changes only through a job, the fix has to be run by hand, ahead of the queue.
prevention: Add a code check that runs when a job fails at its budget cap, and again before a retry. It compares the remaining budget with the stage caps. If the cap is the cause, drain should hold that job with a clear reason, record the cap as the blocker, and queue a budget-raise job for the owner to approve. That job should run ahead of the held job automatically. Drain should not retry under an unchanged cap.
proposed_request: When a job fails twice at its per-job USD budget cap, Athena should stop retrying it under the same cap. Drain should hold the job and record that the cap caused the stop, with the spend per stage. Athena should then produce a budget-raise config job, put it ahead of the held job, and release the held job after that job lands. Acceptance: (1) a test with a job that fails twice at the cap shows drain holds it rather than retrying, and the hold reason names the budget cap; (2) the budget-raise job is queued ahead of the held job; (3) after it lands, the held job is released and runs; (4) a job that fails for a non-budget reason is retried as before. No the person running Athena command is needed in this flow.
